name: markdown-slug-rule
body:
Slug rule — heading text to exactly ONE FQN segment, deterministic (GitHub-style).

NORMALIZATION (the bare slug): trim leading/trailing whitespace; Unicode-normalize (NFC); lowercase (Unicode-aware); replace each whitespace run with a single `-`; drop punctuation except `-` and `_`; preserve non-ASCII letters and digits; collapse runs of `-` and trim leading/trailing `-`. The result cannot contain the `.` separator (`.` is dropped), so a slug never aliases the FQN hierarchy. Normalization alone is not injective across headings, and an empty normalization is not a segment: define bare(h) = normalized(h) when non-empty, else bare(h) = `section`. `section` is the pinned EMPTY-SLUG LITERAL and is an ordinary bare slug that participates in dedup like any other.

DEDUP SPACE — duplicate headings in the SAME document map to distinct segments by construction. Process headings in document order and maintain `assigned`, the set of segments already given out in this document. A heading's segment is the FIRST candidate in its candidate sequence that is not in `assigned`; the chosen candidate is inserted into `assigned` before the next heading. The candidate sequence is generated from the heading's own RAW bare slug `b`:
- `b` not ending in `-<digits>`: `b`, `b-1`, `b-2`, … (bare slug first, then counters);
- `b` ending in `-<digits>`, i.e. `stem-n`: `stem-n`, `stem-(n+1)`, `stem-(n+2)`, … (the trailing number is INCREMENTED; no second counter is appended to the raw slug).

Worked example: `# Overview` -> `overview`; a second `# Overview` (raw `overview`, taken) -> `overview-1`; a following `# Overview 1` (raw `overview-1`, now taken) -> `overview-2`. Candidates are compared against the ASSIGNED set and generated by evolving the RAW slug's own trailing number — the raw-slug candidate space, not the cooked slugs. REJECTED alternatives: appending a counter to the already-cooked slug (would yield `overview-1-1`), and pre-reserving every raw slug (would deny `overview-1` to the second `Overview`).

TOTALITY AND INJECTIVITY: the rule is total (every heading text yields a bare slug; empty -> `section`) and terminating (each candidate sequence is infinite and `assigned` is finite, so a free candidate always exists). Every assigned segment is drawn from the complement of `assigned` and then inserted into it, so no two sections in a document render the same FQN segment — heading -> segment is INJECTIVE within a document. With the unique absolute-path File prefix and a single delimiter-free segment, section FQNs are injective globally, so `claim` never sees a same-kind section collision (which would panic: src/ingest.rs:88-96).

AC: in one document, `# Overview`, `# Overview`, `# Overview 1` render `overview`, `overview-1`, `overview-2`; headings whose normalization is empty render `section`, `section-1`, `section-2`, …; two identical headings render `overview`, `overview-1`. No fixture renders the same segment twice.

The duplicate-heading fixtures are asserted in requirements.requirement.markdown-sections-as-symbols.
